fields.meta_title: Online Daycare Registration Form Builder | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a daycare registration form that counts seats in each age room and takes the registration fee. Every family lands in a database you own.
fields.h1: Build a Daycare Registration Form That Runs Enrollment
fields.hero_description: Describe your rooms and your fees. Emergent builds the daycare registration form, keeps a seat count for each room and records every family who registers.
fields.features_heading: What the Form Handles Before a Child Starts
fields.features_subheading: Each piece below replaces a step a director would otherwise do by hand, one family at a time.
fields.feature_1:
Seats counted for each age room

Set how many children each room takes, such as 8 infants or 12 toddlers. Each child is placed by birth date, and new families move to a waitlist once their room is full.
fields.feature_2:
A registration fee paid at submit

Connect Stripe and collect the registration fee, or the first week of tuition, when the family submits. Each child's row shows what was paid and when, plus any balance due.
fields.feature_3:
Uploads for the records you keep

Add an upload field for each document your program asks for, such as an immunization record or a custody order. Every file is stored on the child's row, next to the answers.
fields.feature_4:
Signed policy acknowledgments

Show the parent handbook and the sick-child policy on the form, each with its own signature box. Each signature is saved with a timestamp and the policy version the parent read.
fields.feature_5:
Reminders for unfinished forms

Pick how long a started form can sit before a nudge goes out. Parents who stop halfway get an email after 3 days, and the director sees every child with a missing item.
fields.feature_6:
Source code in your own repository

Export the whole app to your GitHub repository when a developer wants to extend it with a parent portal or a tuition ledger. You can also publish it on your center's own domain.
fields.why_title: Why Use Emergent for Daycare Registration?
fields.why_description: A printable packet gets one family on paper. It cannot tell the director which rooms are full or whose fee is still unpaid.

fields.usecase_heading: Registration at Four Child Care Programs
fields.tab_content_1:
When cribs run out, families wait by start date

Tallgrass Early Learning keeps 8 cribs in its infant room. Parents register with the baby's birth date and the start date they need. Once all 8 cribs are taken, new families join a waitlist ranked by start date. When a baby moves up to the toddler room, the director offers the open crib to the family at the top of the list.
fields.tab_content_2:
Only a paid fee holds one of six spots

Rosa Delgado runs a family daycare from her home and takes 6 children. Her form collects the child's details and a $75 registration fee through Stripe. A spot counts as held only after the fee clears. A family that leaves before paying holds nothing, and the spot stays open for the next family.
fields.tab_content_3:
A weekly rate from the days a parent picks

Parents at Fernbrook Kids Club pick the afternoons their child attends, at $22 an afternoon. A parent who picks Monday, Wednesday and Friday sees $66 a week before submitting. The club's van collects children at Cedar Park Elementary, and the driver gets a roster for each afternoon.
fields.tab_content_4:
Last year's answers come back for a check

Every spring, Bramble Hill Preschool sends its 42 returning families a link to register for the fall. Their form opens with last year's answers filled in, and parents edit only what changed. By the May 15 deadline, 38 families had confirmed. The 4 seats left over went to the waitlist.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Daycare Registration Form
fields.howto_description: Decide how your rooms and fees work before you write the prompt.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 List your rooms and their ages
fields.howto_step_1_des: Start with the rooms and the ages each one serves, plus how many children it takes. An infant room with 8 cribs and a toddler room with 12 seats are two separate counts. Birth dates decide which room each child goes into.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Note the registration fee first, then whether returning families pay it again and when the first week of tuition is due. Each rule becomes a charge the form collects or a line on the child's record that the director can check later.
fields.howto_step_3_des: List the documents your program keeps for each child, such as an immunization record, a custody order or a doctor's note. If your state licensing agency publishes its own enrollment form, keep its list of questions open beside you while you build.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Paste the room list and the fee rules into the prompt, along with the documents you collect. Emergent builds the form and the payment step, plus the database of children and families behind it. Ask for changes the same way, such as adding a new room.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Give each policy parents must agree to its own screen: the handbook, the sick-child rules, photo permission. Add a signature box under each one. A parent who skips a policy cannot submit the form until that box is signed.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Choose what the form does once a room is full. A waitlist ordered by start date suits an infant room, where babies arrive all year. A program tied to the school year may rank by registration date instead. Write the rule into the prompt.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Fill in the form as a parent would, with a made-up child and a test card for the fee. Check that the child lands in the right room and that the payment shows on the row. Delete the test record before families see the link.

A paper packet records one family, but a director registering children needs more: seats counted per age room, a fee that holds the spot, weekly rates worked out from the days chosen, and last year's families renewing without retyping everything. This page treats registration as the director's enrollment desk and shows four kinds of programs running it.
tab_stories: An infant room with 8 cribs fills up, and the ninth family to register lands on a waitlist ranked by the start date they asked for.

A school-age program lets parents pick afternoons, prices 3 afternoons at $22 each to $66 a week, and gives the bus monitor a roster by day.
A center sends every returning family last year's answers to confirm each spring, and seats not renewed by May 15 go to the waitlist.
